stone_bricks is 56 % of the build: break it up with a second material.

visual.summary: Keep level 3: the same as level 2 with vines climbing the walls.
problems: Level 3 only adds vines over level 2: give it its own feature, such as timber hoardings (wooden galleries) on the towers or steep dark conical roofs on two of them.
It is grey stone brick almost everywhere (56 to 58 %): a dark oak timber element (hoarding, gate canopy, roof) would tie it to the rest of the kingdom's look.
On level 1 the tower tops are open boxes; even a simple slab cap or a stair parapet would make them look finished.

visual.summary: A real castle: a curtain wall with four corner towers and a gatehouse round the keep and great hall, red banners along the walls, kitchen, barracks, a well and gardens inside. One symmetric plan, no longer all over the place.
problems: The turret caps are stepped tiers with a wide flared skirt, which reads more like a pagoda than a medieval tower: make them steep cones (a stair ring with one block of overhang, then 3 or 4 rings narrowing by one each step, finished with a slab and the flagpole), so they are taller than they are wide
The courtyard buildings are hard to see from outside; a lantern or banner on the gatehouse would bring some life to the front
Our QC renders of a structure this big are washed out by fog (renderer, not the build); judged from the near parts

visual.summary: A full castle that makes sense for soldiers: curtain wall with a real wall walk, hollow corner towers with stairs, a gatehouse with a guard chamber, kitchen and armory by the hall, storehouse, guardroom, well and forge by the gate, a flower garden and a training yard. Steep spire roofs, symmetric and coherent.
problems: Reachability (flood fill from the ground outside, soldiers half a block tall, jump 1, drop 3, ladders climb): every floor, room, wall walk and tower top is reached; only the roof cones, the tie beams under the hall roof and the tops of log piles and the low forecourt wall are not, which is right
More life on the outside would help: a few vines or banners on the corner towers
